purpose: Machine-readable signatures that distinguish a verification command that COULD NOT RUN from one that ran and returned a real verdict. ADR-0012 section 5 separates regression from staleness but names only those two outcomes; a build whose target tree was deleted underneath it is neither. Reporting it as a regression points an operator at the claim when the fault is the machine.

contract.fail_closed: An infrastructure classification NEVER writes, refreshes, or promotes evidence. It is strictly a reporting distinction: the claim stays exactly as provisional as it would have been. Nothing here can create evidence.
contract.conservative_default: A non-zero exit that matches no signature is classified as a regression. Misreporting a real regression as infrastructure is the dangerous direction, so the burden of proof sits on the infrastructure claim.
contract.single_match_sufficient: Signatures are disjunctive. The first match decides, so ordering is by specificity.

exit_code_rules.reason: verification command exceeded its timeout and was killed before reaching a verdict

signatures.reason: the linker could not resolve core/alloc intrinsics -- a toolchain or target-tree configuration fault, never a claim regression
signatures.regex: undefined reference to `(core::fmt::write|core::panicking::panic|__rustc::__rust_(alloc|dealloc|no_alloc_shim_is_unstable_v2))|collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status|rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: (core|alloc)::
signatures.provenance: Live 2026-07-26 reproducer. FE-CLAIM-022 was launched with CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointed at a private warm tree, but reemit_evidence_receipts.py overrode it with its own default (./target). That tree is shared with other agents and held rlibs compiled under different RUSTFLAGS, so the nested Node-comparative build failed with `undefined reference to core::fmt::write` and `__rustc::__rust_alloc`. No signature matched, so ADR-0012 5.1's conservative default classified it as a REGRESSION of the lockstep-oracle claim -- exactly the false alarm on the most identity-critical surface that 5.1 exists to prevent. The override is fixed in the same commit; this signature covers the failure mode independently, because a mixed-RUSTFLAGS shared tree can arise without that specific bug.
signatures.why_this_is_never_a_regression: These symbols are emitted by rustc, not by this repository. Engine source cannot cause `core::fmt::write` to be undefined at link time. The narrow anchoring is deliberate per ADR-0012 5.1 point 2: a broad match on `error: could not compile` would excuse real regressions, which is the dangerous direction.

known_divergence.note: scripts/rch_proof_failure_capsule.sh:245 carries its own copy of the target-dir regex and predates this contract. It is the sibling implementation for the rch proof lane and is NOT yet reading this file. Converging it is tracked separately so that a live proof lane is not refactored inside an evidence-freshness change.
